finalText: Ask: run `./slow.sh` and report its output - wanted: its real output and exit code. For you: slow.sh is still in its 90s sleep. I've armed a monitor on the `EXIT=` marker in `out.txt`, and it will wake me when the script finishes. Now: waiting for slow.sh to exit. Next: read `out.txt`, then clean up and complete the goal.

toolArgs.name: eval
create_goal
toolArgs.args: {"objective":"Run ./slow.sh (sleeps ~90s) to completion and report its exact output and exit code. Tier: LIGHT (running an existing script, no edits). Success criterion: run `./slow.sh > $RUN_TMP/out.txt 2>&1` in a background session; PASS = process exits and captured stdout/exit code are read back. Evidence: out.txt contents + exit code. Cleanup: remove $RUN_TMP and confirm no slow.sh process remains. I'll stop right away when slow.sh has exited, its output and exit code are reported, and the cleanup receipt is recorded."}

toolArgs.name: eval
eval
toolArgs.args: {"code":"print(await Bun.$`cat ${RUN_TMP}/out.txt; pgrep -af slow.sh || echo \"no slow.sh process\"`.nothrow().text());","language":"js","summary":"Check slow.sh output and process state"}

toolArgs.name: eval
toolArgs.args: {"code":"const m = await tool.monitor({ description: \"slow.sh exit marker in out.txt\", command: `until grep -q '^EXIT=' ${RUN_TMP}/out.txt; do sleep 3; done; printf 'READY\\\\n'`, filter: \"^READY$\", timeout_ms: 150000 });\nprint(JSON.stringify(m).slice(0,300));","language":"js","summary":"Subscribe to slow.sh exit marker"}

toolArgs.name: eval
toolArgs.args: {"code":"print(await Bun.$`date; cat ${RUN_TMP}/out.txt; pgrep -af 'slow.sh' | grep -v pgrep || echo \"no slow.sh process\"`.nothrow().text());","language":"js","summary":"Check whether slow.sh has finished"}
